synopsis: The safety case organizes claims, arguments and evidence; the plan should be built backwards from the top-level claim to required evidence, methods, credibility levels, work packages and gates, rather than treating a complete scenario spreadsheet as physical evidence [f11298, f9453, f656]. For a four-month validation, the recommended route is an analytical safety case plus targeted physical tests and credibility-qualified simulation; the four months after hardware arrival should include sensor and braking correlation, discrepancy investigation, high-risk physical spot-checks and evidence assembly [f2137, f1596]. The claim spans the full chain from environment and sensing to machine motion and collision outcome, must address both missed and unsafe or unnecessary braking, and should derive its assurance target from the new hazard analysis rather than comparison with the old warning system [f383, f2141, f5816, f10529]. Simulation acceptance requires physical correlation and demonstrated credibility, but model accuracy is not system safety, no mature rule establishes sufficient sim-to-real agreement, and public literature cannot establish whether the proposed plan meets company release criteria [f8341, f7756, f7814, f5071, f4975]. Evidence reuse across machine variants is safety-case-specific and requires explicit transfer justification, configuration-controlled differences and bridging tests where changes affect safety; quantified production precedents for reducing physical validation were not found in the cited forklift, automated guided vehicle and military ground-vehicle cases [f7394, f7045, f7908, f7910, f1413, f1426, f1894]. Safety-case efficacy evidence is mainly case studies and cases can become paperwork, so the argument should disclose validity limits, address operator-dependent protection and be checked against final 2026 standards publications; the general machinery-safety obligation and functional-safety case already exist in 2027 for ML elements [f9451, f9452, f10683, f11807, f11833, f8930, f2380].
